verdict.rationale: iTerm2's first-party docs describe a native tmux integration: `tmux -CC` makes tmux windows behave like native iTerm2 windows. Sessions persist across disconnects and can be reattached with `tmux -CC attach`. The docs also map pane splits onto tmux commands and allow shared sessions between users. missing for 10: independent or hands-on community corroboration of the tmux integration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use tmux inside the terminal, or a documented native tmux integration/control mode

citations.quote: iTerm2 is integrated with tmux, allowing you to enjoy a native user interface with all the benefits of tmux's persistence.
When you run "tmux -CC", a new tmux session is created. An iTerm2 window opens and it acts like a normal iTerm2 window.
You can return to the host you were ssh'ed into and run "tmux -CC attach" and the iTerm2 windows will reopen in the same state they were in before.
Split a pane: Splits the tmux window using the split-window command.
